propositions: The T11 migration rubric's unconditional post-rollback state check generates tautological findings against append-only stores, drowning legitimate data-loss risks in ~38% false positives (8 of 21 sampled).

The post-rollback paragraph must be replaced with a four-condition applicability rule (interpretation change, in-place rewrite/migration, read path removal/narrowing, one-way transformation) that applies across all persistence technologies without naming store-specific implementations.

Purely additive backward-compatible changes (new record types, optional fields, new tables/columns with defaults) must be explicitly exempted from post-rollback findings to avoid false positives in systems that tolerate residual data by design.
The applicability rule and anti-false-positive line must be portable across SQL migrations, event stores, document databases, and config formats without store-technology-specific language.
